column1: # Official media to fetch from the Internet Archive and, when asked, extract
# name <TAB> archive.org item <TAB> file pattern <TAB> corpus output dir <TAB> action [<TAB> exclude regex]
# A push that changes this file starts .github/workflows/import-media.yml,
# which fetches every entry that is not fetched yet, inventories it, and
# imports the documentation pages of the entries whose action is `import`
# or `import-scratch`; already fetched media is never downloaded twice and an
# already extracted component is skipped.
#   inventory        download (if needed) + list what the medium holds
#   import           ... and copy its documentation into the corpus; the
#                    medium is kept verbatim under sources/<name>/ with a
#                    PROVENANCE.md
#   import-scratch   ... and copy its documentation into the corpus; the
#                    medium is fetched to .cache/media/ and thrown away again
#                    (an InstallShield-era installer disc is ~40 MB of mostly
#                    binaries and samples - the corpus keeps pages, not media)
#   inventory-scratch
#                    download and list what the medium holds, then throw the
#                    medium away: for a disc that is only being considered
# A finished import is recorded in data/reports/media-imported.tsv, so a later
# run does not download an image it has already imported (the scratch medium is
# gone by then); `--force` overrides it.
# Either way only documentation is imported: this is a documentation corpus,
# so a medium's source files, headers, samples and toolchains are counted in
# the inventory and skipped (see "What is collected" in the top-level README).
# The 6th field refuses documentation files that are not documentation of the
# product: the exclude below drops infoview.hlp, the SDK disc's 1,236-page help
# for the InfoViewer/Visual C++ viewer UI itself (dialog boxes, wizard fields,
# editor options).  It is Microsoft help, but it is not Windows CE material.
# windbg.hlp (the CE debugger reference) and the disc's readme stay.
# windows-ce-2.0-sdk: Microsoft Windows CE Platform SDK (H/PC) 2.0 (02/98) -
# the CE 2.0 SDK whose Books Online the corpus has been looking for since the
# CE 2.0 Technical Information CD turned out to carry no API reference (see
# sources/windows-ce-2.0/PROVENANCE.md).  The disc is an InstallShield
# installer: the documentation is inside data1.cab/_sys1.cab, which the
# workflow unpacks with `unshield` (7z cannot read InstallShield cabinets).
# The first import attempt downloaded and inventoried the disc but imported
# nothing (7z cannot read those cabinets, and the inventory then crashed on the
# extensionless files of the disc - fixed in tools/import-media.py).
# 2026-10-20: the Books Online proper is InfoViewer titles (.ivt, 11 books
# under data1/Online_help_files/; the .ivi siblings are index-only), for
# which no decoder existed here until tools/extract-ivt.py.  The import
# record was cleared and the medium re-imported the same day: 5,085 pages
# (WCESDK 2,817 + WCESDKG 618 + WCEDDK 323 + the CPU books + WINDBG).
# The first re-run failed the alias check (re-decoding WINDBG resurrected
# a collapsed page); import-media.py's help-file route now holds
# collapsed pages back, as the page and CHM routes already did.
windows-ce-2.0-sdk
# The DevCon '99 conference CD (1999): the Windows CE Developers Conference
# disc.  338 MB / 1,689 files; the disc carries the Windows CE 2.11/2.12 SDK,
# DDK and Platform Builder documentation (wcesdkr/, wceddk/, wcesdkg/,
# wceapc/, ...) next to the conference's own material, and only the
# documentation of the product is imported:
#   * the whole conference folder (Windows_CE_Developers_Conference_..._CD/)
#     is refused - it is the sponsors' shop window (Kingston, Casio, Compaq,
#     ... press releases and product sheets), the Win32/ATL sample trees and
#     their readme pages, not Microsoft documentation of Windows CE;
#   * MPLAYER2/ is the Books Online of the desktop Windows Media Player 2,
#     MPSUPP/ is the generic Microsoft Product Support Services guide,
#     ACCESSIB/ is Microsoft's general accessibility material and Handhelds/
#     is a vendor's Palm-size PC specification sheets - none of them document
#     Windows CE;
#   * FrontPage metadata directories (_vti_cnf/ and friends) are refused by
#     tools/import-media.py itself.
# With those out, the import brings in the CE 2.11/2.12 SDK documentation
# (6,382 pages; see corpus/msdn-library/wcedevcon-99/PROVENANCE.md).
# The first import run died at its first CHM (tools/extract-chm.py is loaded by
# path now, and the workflow caches .cache/media so a retry does not fetch the
# 338 MB image again).
wcedevcon-99
# --- 2026-10-20 harvest expansion: inventory first ---------------------------
# The four media below are the candidates sources/README.md has carried
# since 2026-10; the archive.org identifiers and file forms were
# verified against the item pages on 2026-10-20 (see
# docs/cegcc-survey.ja.md's harvest notes and queues/third-party-sources.md).
# All four enter as inventory-scratch: download, list what the medium
# holds (the listing lands in data/reports/media-last.txt), discard.
# Whether any documentation is imported -- and with which exclude
# regex -- is decided only after reading that inventory.
# CAUTION (standing rule): the Platform Builder discs also carry
# shared-source trees and SDK headers.  Those are never corpus
# material (docs/COLLECTION-POLICY.md: documentation only; the
# importer counts and skips source/binaries, and check-policy.py
# keeps the source-or-binary count at 0).  Only documentation pages
# (HTML/CHM doc sets) may ever flip one of these rows to import.
# windows-ce-5.0-cd5: INVENTORIED 2026-10-20, nothing to import.
# Item en_win_ce_net_cd5 (478.8 MB ISO) holds 18,798 files and zero
# documentation pages (0 HTML / 0 WinHelp / 0 CHM): it is a binaries
# disc (.res/.lib/.pdb/.def/.dll).  Row removed so future runs do
# not fetch it again; the listing is in git history of
# data/reports/media-last.txt (run 39363624759).
# windows-embedded-ce-6.0-r2 / -r3 / -pb-sp1: INVENTORIED 2026-10-20,
# nothing to import.  CE6R2.iso (item windows-embedded-ce-6.0-r2,
# 26,811 files), CE6R3.iso (item CE6R3, 19,745 files) and the PB 6.0
# SP1 package (item windows-embedded-ce-6.0-platform-builder-sp1,
# 3,326 files) are product payloads -- .lib/.pdb/.res/.dll plus
# shared source (.h/.c/.cpp) and MSI internals -- with no
# documentation sets aboard (0 CHM/WinHelp; 3-4 stray HTML installer
# pages only; no .hxs either).  The CE 6.0 documentation itself lived
# in the MSDN Library / Learn sets the corpus already has.  Rows
# removed so future runs do not fetch ~3 GB again; listings are in
# the git history of data/reports/media-last.txt (run 39364902845).
# (2026-10-20: the push trigger in .github/workflows/import-media.yml was
# restored to match the header above -- this edit starts the inventory
# run for the four media added today.)
# MSDN Library for Visual Studio 2008 SP1 (November 2008), pinned
# 2026-10-20 (see sources/README.md).  Inventory only: the disc is
# mostly desktop documentation, which this corpus does not collect,
# so nothing may import until the inventory shows how the Windows
# Mobile / CE content is packaged (loose HTML or MS Help 2 .HxS)
# and an exclude regex can keep an import to that part.  The same
# disc (X15-06188) is officially downloadable from Microsoft
# Download Center id 20955, which pins the item's provenance.
# The first inventory read exactly one file (README.TXT): the disc
# is UDF-mastered and tools/iso9660.py saw only its ISO 9660 stub.
# import-media.py now detects the UDF volume recognition sequence
# and leaves such images to 7z.  The retry saw the real disc: an
# MSI payload whose 42 Microsoft cabinets hold MS Help 2 titles
# under installer names (FL_..._hxs_enu).  The full listing (run
# 39398893470, in the history of data/reports/media-last.txt)
# names 1,268 HxS titles, of which these are the CE ones:
# the whole CE 5.0 set (wcecoreos5, wceddk5, wcecomm5,
# wceinternet5, wcemultimedia5, wcesecurity5, wceshellui5,
# wcefonts5, wceinternational5, wcedata5, wcehardware5,
# wceosdev5, wcedebug5, wceappservices5, wceappenduser5,
# wceappdev5, wcedevicemgt5, wcefeatures5, wcehowto5, wceintro5,
# wcemigrate5, wcepbguide5, wcesamples5, wcetarget5,
# wcevoipsvc5, wcewatson5, wce_devcompiler, _toc_wince50) and,
# the real prize, mobilesdk5 -- the Windows Mobile 5.0 SDK set
# whose bb* topics never migrated to Learn -- plus the managed
# fxref_microsoft.windowsmobile.* titles.  Next step is HxS
# support in the media lane (route the payloads like CHM via 7z,
# scope with an exclude lookahead).  That support landed
# 2026-10-21 (import-media help2_title + extract-chm's shared 7z
# container path), so this entry now imports: the exclude is a
# keep-only lookahead over the title list above, everything else
# on the disc (the desktop library, its installers and samples)
# stays out.  The first import run read every title as 0 pages:
# 7-Zip chooses its HXS handler by extension/type and the MSI
# payload names have neither, so extract_hxs now forces -tHxs and
# presents the title under an .hxs name; the 0-page import record
# was cleared for this retry.
msdn-library-vs2008-sp1

# --- Scouting wave of 2026-10-21: six media pinned and inventoried
# together (full file listings) to decide imports.  MSDN Library
# discs are mostly desktop documentation, so like the VS2008 disc
# above they import nothing until their CE titles are named and an
# exclude can scope an import to them.  The SDK installers are
# documentation-only here too: the lane reads their pages and
# discards the rest (headers and binaries never enter the corpus).
# MSDN Subscriptions Library January 2002: the first Help 2.0

# titles, of which the CE set is WCE* (WCESDKR, WCECOMM, WCEDDK,
# WCEMFC, WCEATL, ... 22 titles), ADOCE31, DNAPPCOM, DNCE21 and
# DNCE30.  This entry imports exactly those.
msdn-library-jan-2002

msdn-library-vsnet2003-d1
msdn-library-vsnet2003-d2

windows-mobile-sdk-bundle

msdn-library-vs2005

msdn-library-jan-2008
